display.purpose: Page titles in the page head, including a record's code on its own page.

headline.purpose: Figure values in the figure strip only.

body.purpose: Every cell, field, list and paragraph; row codes at 650.

variation.purpose: The signed figure of a variation marker.

shadows.name: panel

shadows.name: lift

shadows.name: lift-lg
shadows.purpose: Storefront only: the open category menu, the shared confirmation dialog and toasts. The panel strips it; not a panel precedent.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focused text fields, with a volt border.

shadows.name: flow-card
shadows.purpose: The home's example-order card, on 94% white; floats at rest.

shadows.name: floating-photo
shadows.purpose: The hero's drifting product photos, inside a 4px white frame.

shadows.name: search-halo
shadows.purpose: Focus on the hero search; the header search uses var(--volt-soft) with a volt border.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background changes on buttons and fields.

motion.name: dialog-in
motion.purpose: Confirmation dialog enters from 8px below at 0.98 scale.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Toast drops 8px into place; it leaves sideways in 0.18s.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition. The home's example order becomes a static list of its five states and the floating photos stand still.

motion.name: card-hover
motion.purpose: Product card shadow and border on hover; its photo scales to 1.04 over 0.3s ease.

motion.name: hero-float
motion.purpose: Floating photos rise 8-12px and swing 2deg, each on its own period.

motion.name: flow-loop
motion.purpose: Example order: a step enters from 14px below at 0.98 scale (ease-out), holds, leaves 6px up; the track fills segment by segment.

motion.name: flow-pop
motion.purpose: Each step's badge pops in as the step appears.

motion.name: flow-truck
motion.purpose: The truck rides the violet road from left to right in the shipping step.

narrative.northStar: The Price Bulletin (Boletín de precios); storefront: The Market Canvas (La lona del mercado)
narrative.overview:
The staff panel (`/panel/` and `/catalogo/admin/`) reads like the daily wholesale price bulletin printed for a Colombian food market: white sheets ruled in 1px hairlines, rows grouped under solid forest bands, tabular figures in every column, and each key figure printed beside its variation against a reference. The density is deliberate. Staff work through tens of thousands of orders, customers and SKUs, so rows sit on 8px of padding, structural labels are small condensed caps, and nothing on the page is ornament. A forest rail on the left and a white bar holding one global search frame every page.

The colour is flat and committed. An eleven-step green ramp supplies every neutral, the action green marks what can be clicked, lime marks what is current, and rose, amber, sky, violet and leaf speak only for state. Depth comes from hairlines and solid fills, never from shadows or gradients. Sheets are square; controls take small 3-6px corners. The panel refuses the usual admin template of floating metric cards above one generic table.

The panel scopes its own world under the `panel-app` body class and restyles the shared components (`static/css/components/`) in `static/css/panel/`. The storefront is a second world on the same token file (`static/css/tokens.css`).

The storefront sits under a market stall's canvas. A scalloped hem of action green and lime stripes runs under the header on every customer page, and the home hero stands on wide stripes of pale canvas. A few real product photos drift slowly over those stripes, and a light card plays an example order through its five real states, from cart to delivered. Everything below is honest stock: square white product cards that state the units in the warehouse, a lime chip counting the products of every category, and only the categories and products that exist today. Bricolage Grotesque, narrowed and heavy, sets the headings and prices; Figtree sets the text at 15px. Corners are round (8, 14 and 22px, and pills), and a soft green-tinted shadow lifts a card on hover.

The home, the product catalog and the category index carry this system, approved on 2026-10-23. Pages not yet restyled (cart, checkout, account, order detail) still wear the earlier "fresh market" styling on the same tokens. The user rejected the "mercado campesino" storefront trial (slate green, kraft-paper tags, scalable section index, its animated hero) on 2026-10-22; it stays out of both worlds. The motion the home does have, the example-order loop and the drifting photos, is what the user asked for afterwards.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled sheets, not cards: a 1px g3 hairline around and between modules, g2 inside them, square corners.
One green ramp (g0-g10) for every neutral; volt for actions, lime for the current item.
Archivo throughout: normal width for reading, condensed caps for structure, tabular figures everywhere.
Every key figure carries a signed variation against a stated reference.
The same task works on a phone: ledgers fold into label/value rows and no page scrolls sideways.
Storefront: a scalloped volt and lime awning hem under the header, and market-canvas stripes behind the home hero.
Storefront: square white product cards that state their stock, and a lime chip that counts every category.
Storefront: an example order cycles its five real states, each in its status hue, and stills to a list under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Ramp-Only Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in the panel comes from g0-g10: text, hairlines, row hover, chip fills, the rail. A new tone is taken from the ramp, not mixed. g6 and lighter fail 4.5:1 on white, so they never carry text; body copy is g10 and secondary copy g7.

rules.name: The Lime Marks Now Rule
rules.body: Lime marks the current or selected thing: the brand mark, the square beside the active rail link, the count inside a group band, selected text. In the panel it never fills a button or a surface.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Rose, amber, sky, violet and leaf appear only as state: status chips, variation markers, the low-stock count, errors. They never decorate a section, a heading or a figure that is not reporting a state.

rules.name: The Lime Counts Rule
rules.body: In the storefront lime fills small things that count or confirm: count chips, count badges, the payment-approved chip, and half of the awning's stripes. It always carries ink text and never fills a page section, a card or the primary action, which stays action green.

rules.name: The Condensed Caps Rule
rules.body: Condensed caps label structure: column heads, group bands, figure labels, rail group names. They never set a heading, a sentence or a button, and never sit above a page title.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: The whole panel sets `tabular-nums`. Numeric columns are right-aligned so digits stack, and signed variations use a real minus sign (−), not a hyphen.

rules.name: The Narrowed Heading Rule
rules.body: Only headings shout: the hero, page titles and category names set Bricolage at 800 on a narrowed width (80-85) with tight tracking. Prices stay at 600 and normal width, and running text is always Figtree.

rules.name: The No Sideways Page Rule
rules.body: No panel page scrolls horizontally on a phone. Ledgers fold into label/value rows instead of scrolling, so every ledger cell except the lead one carries a `data-label`.

rules.name: The Joined Module Rule
rules.body: Related figures and controls share one container divided by hairlines: the figure strip, the status tabs, the pagination bar under its ledger. Modules are never separated by air and floated as cards.

rules.name: The Real Shelf Rule
rules.body: The storefront shows only what exists: the home lists only categories that have active products, most products first, and inside each only products in stock; the count in the lead and on every chip is the real one. No banner carousel, no wall of category icons, no invented delivery times, reviews or best sellers.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Panel surfaces are flat at rest and on hover. A module separates from its neighbour by a hairline, never by a shadow or a gradient.

rules.name: The Lift On Response Rule
rules.body: In the storefront a surface lifts only in response: a product card on hover, a menu or dialog when open. Only the hero's example-order card and floating photos float at rest.

rules.name: The Drawn Marker Rule
rules.body: Triangles and chevrons are drawn with CSS `clip-path` in `currentColor`, never typed as glyphs (▲ ▼ →) or pulled from an icon font.

rules.name: The Painted Canvas Rule
rules.body: The awning hem and the canvas stripes are drawn with gradients and a mask, never an image. The hem appears once per page, under the storefront header; the staff console header drops it.

dos: Do take every new neutral from `--g0`..`--g10`; text on white is g7 or darker.
Do print each key figure beside its variation against a named reference, in a right-aligned variation column or a figure note.
Do join related figures, tabs and pagination into one hairline-divided container.
Do lead every ledger row with the record's code, linked, and give every other cell a `data-label`.
Do keep sheets square with a 1px g3 border, and controls at 6px (4px for small pieces, 3px for chips).
Do grow every panel control to 44px under 700px.
Do scope panel styling under `.panel-app` in `static/css/panel/`, loaded after the shared components.
Do keep the scalloped awning hem under the storefront header and the canvas stripes behind the home hero.
Do open the home with the H1 and put the product count in bold at the start of the lead.
Do show only categories that have products, most products first, and on the home only products in stock.
Do use real product photos only: on cards, in the example order, in the floating hero tiles.
Do keep each order state in its status hue wherever the order flow is shown: sky for preparing, violet for shipped.
Do give every storefront animation a reduced-motion state that still shows its content.
Do count with lime pills and ink text.
donts: Don't float metric cards separated by air above one generic table.
Don't add shadows or gradients to panel surfaces, or a press offset to panel buttons.
Don't fill a button or a surface with lime in the panel.
Don't use rose, amber, sky, violet or leaf except to report a state.
Don't set headings, sentences or buttons in condensed caps, or put a caps line above a page title.
Don't type arrows or triangles as glyphs; draw them with `clip-path`.
Don't let a ledger scroll the page sideways on a phone.
Don't bring the storefront's Bricolage Grotesque, Figtree, 14px and 22px corners or lift shadows into the panel.

Don't reuse the rejected "mercado campesino" trial (slate green, kraft-paper tags, scalable section index, its animated hero). The home's example-order loop and drifting photos are the motion the user asked for later.
Don't put an eyebrow, kicker or pill above a storefront H1.
Don't put a banner carousel or a wall of category icons on the home, or invent delivery times, reviews or best sellers.
Don't add a second search field to the home; the hero's search replaces the header's there.
Don't fill a card, a section or the primary action with lime.
Don't extend the earlier "fresh market" styling of the cart, checkout, account and order pages to new screens.
